label: CJEU C-582/14 — Breyer (dynamic IPs as personal data)
body: 1. A dynamic IP address registered by an online media services provider when a person accesses a publicly accessible website is personal data in relation to that provider where the provider has the legal means reasonably likely to be used to identify the subject with additional data held by the ISP.
2. Art. 7(f) precludes national legislation that limits the LI basis to specific-use-of-services purposes; LI may also justify processing for the general operability of services after consultation.
Why it matters: Confirms the relative/contextual test for "personal data" — identifiability is judged by means reasonably likely to be used, not absolute possibility.
